newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Irish March consumer prices rise 0.1 pct m/m - CSO.
newsitem.headline: Irish March consumer prices rise 0.1 pct m/m - CSO.

text.p: Irish inflation, as measured by the consumer price index, showed a month-on-month rise of 0.1 percent in March, the Central Statistics Office said on Thursday.
Most analysts expected a monthly rise of 0.3 percent after a 0.6 percent increase in February for a year-on-year rise of 1.5 percent.
A comparable monthly estimate for March 1996 is not available as Ireland's CSO only began publishing monthly consumer price data in January 1997.
The March CPI was up 0.2 percent for the four months from November and was up 1.6 percent for 13 months from February last year.
The European Union harmonised index of consumer prices (HICP), which is used for intra-EU comparisons, showed no change for the month and was up 1.7 for the 13 months from February last year.
